title: Vijitha Herath expresses condolences over death of Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
byline: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath has expressed his condolences to the Royal Family of Dubai and the people of Dubai following the death of Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

title: Record-Breaking El Niño Surpasses Previous Benchmarks
byline: While forecasts had consistently indicated that 2026 could see an unprecedented El Niño, the latest observations confirm sea-surface temperatures in the central equatorial Pacific have now surpassed levels recorded during any previous event. This milestone represents a significant moment and is likely to have far-reaching impacts on weather patterns around the world.

title: British father admits causing toddler son’s death after fall from Cyprus hotel
byline: A British father has admitted to causing the death of his son while on holiday in Cyprus. The man from Essex was charged with causing death by a reckless act after the toddler fell from the fourth floor of the King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort in Chlorakas on 12 July.

title: 15 found guilty, 9 acquitted in Easter Sunday terror case
byline: Seven years after the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks, 15 of the 24 accused standing trial on 23,270 charges, including conspiring to carry out suicide terrorist attacks targeting tourist hotels, churches and other locations in Colombo and several other areas, and providing assistance and support for the attacks, were found guilty.

title: Heavy rainfall above 100mm expected in several areas
byline: Heavy rainfall exceeding 100mm is expected in several parts of Sri Lanka as the depression currently located over the northwest Bay of Bengal, northeast of the island, is forecast to intensify into a deep depression within the next 12 hours.

title: Police probe Wimal’s remarks over possible contempt of court
byline: The Central Crime Investigation Bureau (CCIB) has launched an investigation into former Minister Wimal Weerawansa following a Colombo Magistrate’s Court order to determine whether remarks he had made at an SLPP rally in Anuradhapura amounted to contempt of court.

title: President recommends two High Court judges for Court of Appeal
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s recommendation to appoint High Court Judges Navaratne Marasinghe and Manjula Thilakaratne as Judges of the Court of Appeal has been forwarded to the Constitutional Council.

title: Referendum cannot be called as a result of protests: Nalinda Jayatissa
byline: A referendum cannot be called as a result of protests or public demonstrations against the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said today.

title: Ex-Western Province Health Minister arrested
byline: Former Western Province Provincial Health Minister Angage Jagath Thilakasiri Perera has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over alleged bribery charges.

title: New Irrigation DG appointed
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the appointment of Engineer P.M. Jayadeera as the new Director General of Irrigation, effective from October 6, 2026.

title: Cabinet approves €4.93 million contract for 5 million NIC cards
byline: Cabinet approval has been granted to award a contract for the procurement of five million pre-printed polycarbonate cards required for the issuance of National Identity Cards (NICs).

title: 133 construction workers to leave for Israel tomorrow
byline: A total of 133 Sri Lankan construction job seekers are scheduled to leave for Israel tomorrow (23) for employment in the country’s construction sector, the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) said.

title: Navy builds Sri Lanka’s first waveless referee boat
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has designed and built the country’s first waveless referee boat for rowing and canoeing competitions at the Navy Water Sports Centre in Diyawanna, Battaramulla.

title: SLINEX-26 ends with joint naval drills
byline: The 13th edition of the Sri Lanka–India naval exercise, SLINEX-26, concluded successfully in Visakhapatnam on September 21, 2026, strengthening maritime cooperation and operational coordination between the two navies.

title: President telling new lies to mark second anniversary: Namal
byline: SLPP MP Namal Rajapaksa accused President Anura Kumara Dissanayake of travelling across the country and telling “new lies,” claiming that the Government has little to show for its achievements over the past two years.

title: Flights at major US airports delayed after cable cut by construction workers
byline: Hundreds of flights have been delayed at major airports in the US after construction workers accidentally cut a cable needed for air traffic control.

title: China company wins US$40.84M Muthurajawela aviation fuel contract
byline: China Petroleum Pipeline Engineering Company Limited has been awarded a major contract worth US$40.84 million and Rs. 8,548.75 million to develop a new aviation fuel storage and distribution facility at Muthurajawela.

title: Bring reusable bags to Colombo Book Fair, CEA urges public
byline: The Central Environmental Authority (CEA) has urged consumers visiting the Colombo International Book Fair to bring an environmentally friendly, reusable bag to carry the books they purchase and contribute to protecting the environment.

title: Mustapha, Kumarapperuma offer free legal assistance in Anojan’s case
byline: President’s Counsel Faiszer Musthapha and President’s Counsel Upul Kumarapperuma have agreed to provide legal assistance in the case of Sri Lankan national Sivarasa Anojan, who was sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath told Parliament today.

title: New Sri Lanka Cricket Bill gets Cabinet nod
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the publication of a new Sri Lanka Cricket Bill aimed at reorganizing and strengthening the administration of cricket in the country.

title: State to take ownership of Neville Fernando Hospital, Air Force to manage
byline: The Government is set to take full ownership of the Dr. Neville Fernando Teaching Hospital (NFTH), with the Sri Lanka Air Force entrusted with its day-to-day management under a new hybrid operational framework approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

title: India crush Sri Lanka to retain Asian Games Gold
byline: India retained the Asian Games women’s cricket gold medal with a commanding 147-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final at the Aichi Prefectural Korogi Sports Park on Tuesday. The defending champions produced a dominant all-round performance to secure their second consecutive Asian Games title.

title: Seat belts help reduce expressway accident casualties: RDA
byline: Road Development Authority (RDA) Director General Anuradha Hettiarachchi said yesterday that casualties from road accidents on expressways have declined following the introduction of mandatory seat-belt regulations for all passengers.

title: ‘Walk the talk’ on justice for Sri Lankan fishermen, Chandrasekar tells Vijay
byline: In response to Tamil Nadu fishermen’s continued poaching in Sri Lankan waters, Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar said he had conveyed a message to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, asking him to “walk the talk,” as a former actor who fought for justice through his cinematic roles, and ensure it for Sri Lankan fishermen.

title: Supreme Court determines Clause 17 of Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill requires referendum
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramarathne informed Parliament today that the Supreme Court has determined that Clause 17 of the “Anti-Corruption (Amendment)” Bill is inconsistent with Article 4(c) of the Constitution and is required to be passed with the Special Majority required under Article 84(2) and approved by the People at a referendum in terms of Article 83 of the Constitution.

title: Sri Lankan-origin actress will play Sita in a leading musical at Wembley Arena
byline: Sri Lankan-origin actress Bhavithra Gananathan is set to make her professional acting debut as Sita in the major arena production Diwali Story: The Journey of Ram – A Musical at OVO Arena Wembley on Sunday, 27 September 2026.

title: Easter Sunday attacks case judgment proceedings begin
byline: The case against 24 accused, including Naufer Moulavi, over 23,270 charges relating to conspiring, aiding and abetting suicide terrorist attacks targeting tourist hotels, churches and other locations in Colombo and several other areas on Easter Sunday in 2019 commenced at around 12.20 p.m. today for the pronouncement of the judgment.

title: Fitch upgrades Sri Lanka’s rating to ’B-’
byline: Global ratings agency Fitch upgraded Sri Lanka’s long-term foreign-currency default rating to ’B-’ from ’CCC+’ on Tuesday and kept its outlook stable, citing policies and structural reforms that have eased external financing risks.

title: Russian Embassy hosts polling station for State Duma election
byline: A polling station had been set up at the Russian Embassy in Colombo last Sunday for Russian nationals, particularly embassy staff members, to cast their ballots at the election to the State Duma, the Russian Parliament.

title: Committee proposes community service, work camps to ease prison overcrowding
byline: Officials have proposed referring minor offenders serving sentences of less than four years, or those unable to pay relatively small fines, to community service or work camps through expedited judicial procedures as part of measures to ease severe overcrowding in Sri Lankan prisons.

title: 15 convicted in Easter Sunday case, each handed 220-year sentence
byline: The High Court Trial-at-Bar today sentenced each of the 15 accused found guilty in the Easter Sunday terror case to 220 years of rigorous imprisonment.

title: Was negligence behind former Ampara hospital director’s death?
byline: A Health Ministry investigation into the treatment of a patient who later died at the Sri Jayewardenepura General Hospital has raised serious questions over the medical and nursing procedures followed during the patient’s treatment, according to the investigation report.

title: Certain passengers exempt from seat-belt requirement on expressways: Police
byline: Certain passengers are exempt from the mandatory seat-belt requirement on expressways under the relevant Gazette notification, Police said.

title: Water supply to be suspended in several Anuradhapura areas tomorrow
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced that the water supply to several areas in Anuradhapura will be temporarily suspended for eight hours tomorrow (23).
